public_task_requirement: Please implement a website for The All-In Bourbon Bar to showcase its products and services. The website should have functionalities for displaying menus, introducing the membership-only private poker room, and showcasing events and promotions. Users should be able to browse the website, view menus, learn about the private poker room, view events and promotions, and make online reservations or purchases. Use peach puff for container backgrounds and indian red for component visuals.

task_summary.requirement_coverage: The site was intended to showcase The All-In Bourbon Bar with menu browsing, a members-only poker room, events/promotions, and online reservations or purchases, using peach puff container backgrounds and indian red component visuals. Verified coverage includes a visible menu section, a private poker room information section, and an events/promotions section with RSVP buttons. The main functional gap is the reservation/purchase flow: the evaluation agent could not reach a reservation form or confirmation after interacting with RSVP controls, so the online reservation/purchase requirement was not fully demonstrated.
verified_strengths: Menu content is present with item names, descriptions, and prices.
The members-only poker room section is implemented and reachable from navigation.
Events and promotions are displayed with dated entries and RSVP buttons.
The requested color palette is reflected in the rendered pages, with peach puff containers and indian red accents visible in the evaluated screenshots.
primary_functional_risks: The RSVP interaction did not produce a reservation form or confirmation within the interaction budget, so the reservation/purchase path may be incomplete or non-functional.
The implementation appears tab-based and may require explicit navigation to expose all required sections, which can hide content from the initial view.
The evaluation evidence suggests the page state can remain on the events list without progressing to a booking flow, indicating a likely missing state transition or handler.
primary_visual_observations: The screenshot-based appearance feedback reported no obvious rendering errors and confirmed the requested colors were used.
The first visible screen in the appearance review showed the menu section, while the poker room and events content were not visible on that screen.
The layout was described as clean and organized, with legible text and clear component separation.

appearance_reflection.observed_result: The navigation bar has exactly 3 tabs: "Menu", "Poker Room", and "Events & Promotions". The first-screen screenshot review said the page shown was the menu page, and the evaluator noted that there was no visible information about the private poker room or clear links to events and promotions on that first screen. The code shows the poker room content and the events content are each rendered only when their tab is active, because App.vue uses three separate v-if blocks for the three sections.
appearance_reflection.likely_cause_or_limitation: The evidence supports an appearance issue on the first screen: the poker room information and events/promotions links are not visible up front, even though the sections exist and were reached in later tester steps. This is not a missing build feature; it is a visibility/layout problem in the initial view.
appearance_reflection.preventative_action: Make the private poker room information and the events/promotions entry visible on the first screen, with each required section represented by a clear, immediately visible navigation item or preview. Verify that a first-screen render shows the poker room content and a clear path to events/promotions without scrolling or switching away from the initial view.
appearance_reflection.verification: Open the page at the initial load and confirm that the first screen shows the poker room information and a clear events/promotions link or preview without any interaction.
appearance_reflection.transfer_limits: Applies to tabbed or sectioned hospitality sites where required content must be visible from the landing view.

evidence_refs.same_fix: Add the missing private poker room information and clear links to events and promotions.

appearance_reflection.deduction: there is no visible information about the private poker room or clear links to events and promotions
appearance_reflection.group_reason: Add the missing private poker room information and clear links to events and promotions.

functional_reflections.feature_object: making an online reservation or purchase from the events and promotions feature
functional_reflections.user_trigger: Click an RSVP control on an event or promotion item after opening the events and promotions section.
functional_reflections.expected_state_change: The site should open a reservation or purchase flow and then show a visible confirmation after the user submits it.
functional_reflections.observed_result: The tester clicked the RSVP buttons on the event cards, but no reservation form, checkout flow, or confirmation message appeared.
functional_reflections.likely_cause_or_limitation: The events and promotions component only renders static RSVP buttons; the broken sub-step is that clicking a valid RSVP control does nothing and never reveals the reservation flow.
functional_reflections.preventative_action: For any RSVP or purchase button, attach a real interaction handler that opens the reservation or checkout UI and renders a success state after submission. Static buttons should not be the only control exposed for a transactional action.
functional_reflections.verification: After clicking RSVP, the page should visibly change to a form or modal, and submitting it should leave a confirmation message on screen.
functional_reflections.transfer_limits: This reflection is limited to the reservation/purchase action in the events and promotions feature and does not claim anything about the menu, poker room, or site-wide navigation.

{{ event.title }}

Date: {{ event.date }}

{{ event.description }}

evidence_refs.quote: Users should be able to browse the website, view menus, learn about the private poker room, view events and promotions, and make online reservations or purchases.

investigation.task: The check asked whether a user can make an online reservation/purchase from the events and promotions area by using the RSVP controls, and the tester’s final answer was NO because repeated clicks on the RSVP buttons never produced a reservation form or confirmation.
investigation.reached_target: Yes. The trajectory reached the Events & Promotions section and the RSVP buttons on the event cards, so the target feature was exercised rather than abandoned early.
investigation.screenshots: Both screenshots show the Events & Promotions page with two event cards and visible RSVP buttons, but no reservation form, dialog, or success message appears after the clicks.
investigation.code_path: src/App.vue renders <EventsPromotions v-if="activeTab === 'events'" />, and src/components/EventsPromotions.vue contains only static event cards with <button class="reserve-btn">RSVP</button>; there is no click handler, form component, or confirmation state in that feature path.
investigation.style_trace: Not applicable. The screenshots show the RSVP controls and event cards clearly, so this is not a styling/visibility problem.
investigation.candidates: 1) Missing reservation interaction logic: supported by the trajectory showing repeated RSVP clicks with no state change and by EventsPromotions.vue having only a plain button. 2) Unreachable reservation form elsewhere: ruled down because the tester was already on the events section and the screenshots show no alternate reservation UI. 3) Tester limitation: supported only by the interaction budget exhaustion, but the absence of any handler or form in code makes the missing interaction the stronger cause.
investigation.conclusion: The surviving cause is that the Events & Promotions feature has only static RSVP buttons and no implemented reservation flow, so clicking RSVP cannot open a form or confirm a reservation.
investigation.fix_check: Add reservation state and a click handler in src/components/EventsPromotions.vue, or mount a dedicated reservation form/modal from that button, so the RSVP action reveals a form and submits to a visible confirmation. That change alone would satisfy this check because the tester already reached the correct section and the failure is the missing interaction.
investigation.preventative_action: For any button that is meant to start a reservation or purchase flow, wire it to visible UI state: clicking the control should open a form, modal, or checkout panel and submitting it should render a confirmation message in the same feature component.
investigation.verification: Reopen the Events & Promotions section, click an RSVP control, and confirm that a reservation form or confirmation appears without needing to guess another page.
investigation.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to event cards or promotion tiles that advertise RSVP/reservation actions; it does not address unrelated navigation, menu browsing, or poker-room content.
